cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Hello, Picturerep. Can I help you?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh, hi. I saw your advertisement about copying pictures to disk and I’d like a bit more information about what you do.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Sure. What would you like to know?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Well, I’ve got a box full of old family photos that’s been up in the attic for years, some of them must be 50 or 60 years old, and I’d like to get them converted to digital format.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Sure, we can do that for you.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Right. And what about size? The photos are all sorts of sizes - are there any restrictions?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Well the maximum size of photo we can do with our normal services is 30 centimetres. And each picture must be a least 4 centimetres, that’s the minimum we can cope with.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: That should be fine. And some of them are in a frame (Q1) - should I take them out before I send them?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Yes please, we can’t copy them otherwise. And also the photos must all be separate, they mustn’t be stuck into an album.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK, that’s not a problem. So can you give me an idea of how much this will cost? I’ve got about 360 photos I think.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: We charge £195 for 300 to 400 photos (Q2) for the basic service.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK. And does that include the disk?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Yes, one disk - but you can get extra ones for £5 each.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: That’s good. So do I need to pay when I send you the photos?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: No, we won’t need anything until we’ve actually copied the pictures. Then we’ll let you know how much it is, and once we’ve received the payment (Q3), we’ll send the parcel off to you.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Is there anything else you’d like to ask about our services?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Yes. I’ve roughly sorted out the photos into groups, according to what they’re about - so can you keep them in those groups when you copy them?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Sure. We’ll save each group in a different folder on the disk and if you like, you can suggest a name for each folder.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: So I could have one called ‘Grandparents’ (Q4) for instance?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Exactly.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: And do you do anything besides scan the photos? Like, can you make any improvements?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Yes, in the standard service each photo is checked, and we can sometimes touch up the colour a bit (Q5), or improve the contrast - that can make a big difference.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK. And some of the photos are actually quite fragile - they won’t get damaged in the process, will they?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: No, if any look particularly fragile, we’d do them by hand (Q6). We do realise how precious these old photos can be.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Sure.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: And another thing is we can make changes to a photo if you want - so if you want to remove an object from a photo, or maybe alter the background (Q7), we can do that.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Really? I might be interested in that. I’ll have a look through the photos and see. Oh, and talking of fixing photos - I’ve got a few that aren’t properly in focus (Q8). Can you do anything to make that better?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: No, I’m afraid that’s one thing we can’t do.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Any other information I can give you?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Er … oh, how long will it all take?

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: We aim to get the copying done in ten days. (Q9)

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Fine. Right, well I’ll get the photos packed up in a box and post them off to you.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Right. If you’ve got a strong cardboard box, that’s best. We’ve found that plastic ones sometimes break in the post. (Q10)

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK. Right, thanks for your help. Bye.

cues.speaker: EMPLOYEE
cues.text: Bye.
